nodes.description: A parathyroid chief cell, pancreatic islet cell, or anterior pituitary cell now carries no functional MEN1 allele. Menin is a nuclear scaffold with no catalytic activity of its own; the tumor-suppressive function it provides in these lineages is lost as a whole rather than as a single enzymatic step, which is why no one pathway substitutes for it and why the tumors that follow are lineage-defined rather than pathway-defined.

evidence.snippet: By comparing constitutional and tumour tissue genotypes of insulinomas from a pair of brothers who had inherited MEN-1 from their mother, we have shown that oncogenesis in these cases involves unmasking of a recessive mutation at this locus.

nodes.description: A heterozygous loss-of-function variant in MEN1 at 11q13 is present in every nucleated cell of the carrier. MEN1 encodes menin, a nuclear scaffold protein with no similarity to previously characterized proteins, which acts as a tumor suppressor in endocrine tissue. The heterozygous state is compatible with normal endocrine function, so the constitutional lesion is a susceptibility rather than a disease state — what it changes is that every parathyroid, islet, and pituitary cell now sits one event away from complete menin loss.

evidence.reference_title: Positional cloning of the gene for multiple endocrine neoplasia-type 1.
evidence.snippet: DNA sequencing from a previously identified minimal interval on chromosome 11q13 identified several candidate genes, one of which contained 12 different frameshift, nonsense, missense, and in-frame deletion mutations in 14 probands from 15 families.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical practice guidelines for multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1).
evidence.snippet: MEN1 is an autosomal dominant disorder that is due to mutations in the tumor suppressor gene MEN1, which encodes a 610-amino acid protein, menin.

genetic_context.description: Constitutional heterozygous MEN1 loss of function; frameshift, nonsense, missense and in-frame deletion alleles were all identified in the original mutation-positive families.

evidence.reference_title: Positional cloning of the gene for multiple endocrine neoplasia-type 1.
evidence.snippet: The MEN1 gene contains 10 exons and encodes a ubiquitously expressed 2.8-kilobase transcript.

nodes.description: The clinical signature: parathyroid, pancreatic islet and anterior pituitary tumors, with carcinoid, adrenocortical, meningeal and cutaneous lesions in a substantial minority. Tumors in MEN1 carriers behave worse than their sporadic counterparts not because the histology differs but because they are multiple, larger, more often metastatic, and less amenable to the operations that cure the solitary sporadic lesion — the direct clinical expression of the two-hit architecture. Life expectancy is reduced accordingly.

nodes.description: Menin-null cells expand clonally within parathyroid, enteropancreatic and anterior pituitary tissue. Because initiation events are independent, MEN1 parathyroid disease is characteristically an asynchronous multigland process and MEN1 pancreatic neuroendocrine disease is multicentric — a distinction with direct surgical consequence, since resecting one apparently causative lesion leaves the remaining primed tissue behind.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical practice guidelines for multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1).
evidence.snippet: MEN1 is characterized by the occurrence of parathyroid, pancreatic islet, and anterior pituitary tumors.

nodes.description: Surgery for MEN1 hyperparathyroidism is not the single-gland operation used for sporadic disease: because every parathyroid cell carries the first hit and disease is multiglandular, the operation is subtotal parathyroidectomy with cryopreservation, or total parathyroidectomy with autotransplantation. Postoperative hypoparathyroidism is the expected trade-off and must be monitored for. Calcimimetics are the fallback when surgery fails or is contraindicated.

evidence.snippet: Hyperparathyroidism is treated with subtotal parathyroidectomy and cryopreservation of parathyroid tissue or total parathyroidectomy and autotransplantation of parathyroid tissue
calcimimetics are used to treat primary hyperparathyroidism in those for whom surgery is contraindicated or has failed

nodes.description: The concrete protocol behind this entry's surveillance rationale. Surveillance begins in early childhood — age five for calcium, prolactin and IGF-1 — because tumors initiate whenever a second hit occurs rather than at a set age, and continues across several organ systems on different schedules.

evidence.snippet: Annual fasting serum calcium, and consider fasting serum intact PTH from age five years; annual serum prolactin, IGF-1, fasting glucose, and insulin from age five years; head MRI every three to five years from age five years
annual fasting serum gastrin from age 20 years; consider abdominal CT, MRI, or endoscopic ultrasound every three to five years

nodes.description: Because the constitutional allele is present from birth and second hits accumulate over decades, the intervention with the clearest rationale in MEN1 is early identification of carriers followed by biochemical and imaging surveillance, so that tumors are detected before they metastasize.

evidence.snippet: The prognosis for MEN1 patients might be improved by presymptomatic tumor detection and undertaking treatment specific for MEN1 tumors.

nodes.description: A somatic event removes the retained wild-type MEN1 allele in a single endocrine cell, most often as loss of heterozygosity across the 11q13 region. This was demonstrated for MEN1 a decade before the gene was cloned, by comparing constitutional with tumour genotypes in insulinomas from two brothers who had inherited MEN1 from their mother — the tumours showed unmasking of the recessive mutation at the locus. Because the second hit is stochastic and every cell of the target tissue is equally primed, hits occur independently many times over, which is the direct mechanistic reason MEN1 parathyroid and islet disease is multiglandular and multicentric rather than solitary.
